extraction.name: Stanford Question Answering Dataset (SQuAD) v1.0
extraction.description: A reading comprehension dataset consisting of 100,000+ questions posed by crowdworkers on a set of Wikipedia articles, where the answer to each question is a segment of text from the corresponding reading passage.
extraction.creator: Pranav Rajpurkar, Jian Zhang, Konstantin Lopyrev, Percy Liang
extraction.citeAs: Pranav Rajpurkar and Jian Zhang and Konstantin Lopyrev and Percy Liang. 2016. SQuAD: 100,000+ Questions for Machine Comprehension of Text. arXiv:1606.05250v3 [cs.CL]
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was collected in three stages: (1) curating passages from Wikipedia articles, (2) crowdsourcing question-answers on those passages, and (3) obtaining additional answers. Wikipedia articles were retrieved using Project Nayuki's Wikipedia's internal PageRanks to obtain the top 10000 articles, from which 536 articles were sampled uniformly at random. Individual paragraphs were extracted from these articles, stripping away images, figures, tables, and discarding paragraphs shorter than 500 characters, resulting in 23,215 paragraphs.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Over the development and test sets, 2.6% of questions were marked unanswerable by at least one of the additional crowdworkers.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Wikipedia articles retrieved using Project Nayuki's Wikipedia's internal PageRanks to obtain the top 10000 articles of English Wikipedia, from which 536 articles were sampled uniformly at random. Individual paragraphs were extracted, stripping away images, figures, tables, and discarding paragraphs shorter than 500 characters.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: From each of the 536 Wikipedia articles, individual paragraphs were extracted, stripping away images, figures, tables, and discarding paragraphs shorter than 500 characters. The articles were partitioned randomly into a training set (80%), a development set (10%), and a test set (10%).
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Crowdworkers were tasked with asking and answering up to 5 questions on the content of each paragraph. Questions had to be entered in a text field, and answers had to be highlighted in the paragraph. Workers were encouraged to ask questions in their own words, without copying word phrases from the paragraph. Copy-paste functionality on the paragraph text was disabled. Workers spent 4 minutes on every paragraph. For additional answers, crowdworkers were shown only the questions along with the paragraphs and asked to select the shortest span in the paragraph that answered the question. If a question was not answerable by a span in the paragraph, workers were asked to submit the question without marking an answer.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Daemo platform with Amazon Mechanical Turk as its backend
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: To get an indication of human performance on SQuAD and to make evaluation more robust, at least 2 additional answers were obtained for each question in the development and test sets. Human performance was assessed by treating the second answer to each question as the human prediction, and keeping the other answers as ground truth answers. Mismatch occurs mostly due to inclusion/exclusion of non-essential phrases rather than fundamental disagreements about the answer.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: At least 3 answers per question for development and test sets (1 original answer plus at least 2 additional answers)
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Crowdworkers were required to have a 97% HIT acceptance rate, a minimum of 1000 HITs, and be located in the United States or Canada.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Stanford CoreNLP (for constituency parses, POS tags, NER tags, and dependency parse trees)
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Geography (United States or Canada location requirement for crowdworkers)
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: 77.3% of the correct answers in the development set are constituents in the constituency parse, placing an effective ceiling on the accuracy of methods that only consider constituents as candidate answers. The span constraint means that answers are more constrained than interpretative questions found in more advanced standardized tests. Questions with span-based answers focus on answers that are entailed by the passage, whereas answers to cloze-style queries are merely suggested by the passage.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is partitioned into a training set (80%), a development set (10%), and a test set (10%). The dataset is designed for training and evaluating reading comprehension models. The dataset presents a challenge problem for machine comprehension of text, with the goal of advancing natural language understanding.
